title: Error Spotting
intro: Error spotting gives a sentence split into parts and asks which part (if any) has a grammatical error. It is the purest test of grammar rules, and the errors come from a predictable shortlist: subject-verb agreement, wrong tense, wrong preposition, pronoun mismatch, and article misuse. Train yourself to check each part against these rules in order, rather than reading for 'what sounds wrong'.

items.name: Tense
items.formula: time markers must match the verb form

items.name: Pronoun
items.formula: must agree with its noun in number/person

topics.name: Noun & Pronoun Errors
topics.details: Pronouns must agree with the noun they replace in number and person, and be in the right case. 'Each', 'everyone', 'neither' are singular. Some nouns are always plural (scissors) or always singular/uncountable (information, furniture, advice).

solved.problem: Find the error: "Each of the boys have / a book."
Find the error: "She gave the gift to my brother and I."
solved.solution: "I" is wrong — after a preposition use "me".

solved.problem: Find the error: "He gave me many informations."
Find the error: "Neither of them were present."

unsolved.problem: Error: "Everyone must do their / best." (formal singular)
Error: "The furnitures are new."
Error: "Between you and I, it is true."
Error: "One should mind your own business."
Error: "He gave me an advice."
unsolved.answer: "an advice" → advice / a piece of advice

topics.name: Verb & Tense Errors
topics.details: Verbs must agree with the true subject and match the time of the sentence. Find the real subject (not a noun in a phrase between it and the verb). Time markers fix the tense; after modals use the base verb.

solved.problem: Find the error: "The list of items are long."
Find the error: "He has gone to Delhi yesterday."
solved.solution: "has gone" is wrong — "yesterday" needs simple past "went".

solved.problem: Find the error: "She can sings well."
solved.solution: "sings" is wrong — after "can" use base form "sing".

solved.problem: Find the error: "They are living here since 2010."

unsolved.problem: Error: "One of the students were absent."
Error: "I did not went there."
Error: "He is knowing the answer."
Error: "She has come yesterday."
Error: "You must to go now."

topics.name: Preposition & Conjunction Errors
topics.details: Many words take a fixed preposition: good AT, married TO, afraid OF, depend ON, different FROM. Conjunctions come in pairs (not only … but also; neither … nor) that must be used together.

solved.problem: Find the error: "He is good in mathematics."
Find the error: "She is married with a doctor."
Find the error: "Neither he or his friend came."
Find the error: "This is different than that."

unsolved.problem: Error: "I am afraid from dogs."
Error: "We depend in our parents."
Error: "Not only he sings but also dances." (placement)
unsolved.answer: "Not only he sings" → He not only sings

unsolved.problem: Error: "They congratulated me for my success."
Error: "Either you or him is wrong."

topics.name: Article & Modifier Errors
topics.details: Use 'a' before a consonant sound and 'an' before a vowel sound (by SOUND, not letter). Use 'the' for something specific/unique. Avoid double comparatives/superlatives; comparatives need 'than'.

solved.problem: Find the error: "He waited for a hour."
solved.solution: "a hour" is wrong — silent h, vowel sound → "an hour".

solved.problem: Find the error: "She is the more better singer."
solved.solution: "more better" is a double comparative → "the better".

solved.problem: Find the error: "He is an university student."
solved.solution: "an university" is wrong — "university" begins with a "y" sound → "a university".

solved.problem: Find the error: "This is most unique design."
solved.solution: "most unique" is wrong — "unique" is absolute (no degrees).

unsolved.problem: Error: "Sun rises in the east."
Error: "She sings more sweeter than him."
Error: "He is a honest man."
Error: "It is the most cleverest plan."
Error: "I bought a useful umbrella and a apple."

shortcuts: Check each part against the rule list (S-V agreement, tense, pronoun, preposition, article).
Find the real subject — ignore phrases between it and the verb (the list … is).
Time markers fix the tense (since/for → perfect; yesterday → past).
Learn fixed prepositions (good AT, married TO, different FROM).
a/an by SOUND (an hour, a university); avoid double comparatives.
mistakes: Choosing what "sounds wrong" instead of testing a rule.
Matching the verb to a nearby noun rather than the true subject.
Using the wrong half of a correlative pair (neither … or).
a/an by spelling instead of sound.
pyq: SSC error-spotting reliably tests subject-verb agreement, tense with time markers, fixed prepositions and articles. A rule-by-rule scan of each part is faster and surer than reading for feel.
summary: Error spotting is rule-checking, not feel. Scan each part for subject-verb agreement (find the true subject), correct tense (mind time markers), pronoun agreement, fixed prepositions and correct articles (a/an by sound). Watch correlatives (neither…nor) and avoid double comparatives.
